name: @mnema/vscode
description: A VS Code extension for the person who reviews the mnema record: the rules in force over the open file, the decisions waiting for a judgment, the stacks adopted for the project, and where the record verifies. It reads and writes only through the mnema command line and is not published.
author: Felipe Sauer (https://github.com/felipesauer)

mnema.command.markdownDescription: The `mnema` executable the extension runs. It is started directly, with an argument array, never through a shell. Set it in your user settings: a repository's own settings cannot change it.

mnema.stackIndex.markdownDescription: The folder holding the index of stacks (`index.json`), relative to the workspace folder. It is read by `mnema stack index`.

viewsWelcome.contents:
This folder holds no .mnema record, so there is nothing to list. Run mnema init in a terminal here to start one.
[What a first record looks like](https://github.com/felipesauer/mnema/blob/main/docs/first-record.md)

The mnema command could not be used, so nothing is listed: this is not the same as nothing being pending. Install @mnema/code from its source ([how](https://github.com/felipesauer/mnema/blob/main/docs/install.md)), or point the extension at the executable with mnema.command.
[Set the mnema command](command:workbench.action.openSettings?%5B%22mnema.command%22%5D)
[Refresh](command:mnema.refresh)

No decision is listed as awaiting a judgment. If mnema could not run, nothing is listed either, and the status bar says what it read.
[Refresh](command:mnema.refresh)
[Set the mnema command](command:workbench.action.openSettings?%5B%22mnema.command%22%5D)

This folder holds no .mnema record, so no stack is adopted. Run mnema init in a terminal here to start one.
[What a first record looks like](https://github.com/felipesauer/mnema/blob/main/docs/first-record.md)

The mnema command could not be used, so nothing is listed: this is not the same as nothing being pending. Install @mnema/code from its source ([how](https://github.com/felipesauer/mnema/blob/main/docs/install.md)), or point the extension at the executable with mnema.command.
[Set the mnema command](command:workbench.action.openSettings?%5B%22mnema.command%22%5D)
[Refresh](command:mnema.refresh)

No stack is adopted for this project, as mnema stack list reads it.
[Add a stack](command:mnema.stacks.add)
[Add a stack from the index](command:mnema.stacks.addFromIndex)

mnema has not listed the stacks. If it could not run, the status bar says what it read.
[Refresh](command:mnema.refresh)
[Set the mnema command](command:workbench.action.openSettings?%5B%22mnema.command%22%5D)

walkthroughs.title: Get started with mnema
walkthroughs.description: Three steps: make the command available, start a record, run mnema verify.

steps.title: Make the mnema command available
steps.description:
The extension runs the mnema command line and nothing else. Install @mnema/code from its source, or set the executable the extension starts.
[Open the mnema.command setting](command:workbench.action.openSettings?%5B%22mnema.command%22%5D)

steps.title: Start a record in this project
steps.description:
Run mnema init in a terminal at the project root. It creates the .mnema folder where the record is kept.
[Open a terminal](command:workbench.action.terminal.new)

steps.title: Run mnema verify and read what it prints
steps.description:
Run mnema verify in the terminal. It prints the level it reached and what that level covers. The status bar shows that level and nothing more.
[Open a terminal](command:workbench.action.terminal.new)
[Refresh the status bar](command:mnema.refresh)
